method.name: CoreNetClockNow
method.brief: Monotonic seconds, for driving a clock where there is no frame to take a delta from.

return.description: Seconds since an unspecified point, increasing.

method.description: A dedicated server has no window, so raylib's GetTime -- which the windowed engine loop uses -- is not available to it. This is the same measurement without one: monotonic, so it never jumps when the wall clock is adjusted, and with an arbitrary origin, so only differences mean anything.

return.description: True on success; false when an argument is unusable, leaving the clock zeroed.

param.name: tickRate
param.description: Simulation steps per second; must be positive.

param.name: sendRate
param.description: Snapshots per second; clamped to at most tickRate, since a snapshot of a step that has not been simulated has nothing new in it.

method.name: CoreNetClockAdvance
method.brief: Adds real time and reports how many fixed steps are now due.

return.description: Number of fixed steps to run now. Call CoreNetClockTicked once per step run.

param.name: maxTicks
param.description: Ceiling on the steps returned, so a long stall cannot demand an unbounded catch up; the unrun time is discarded rather than accumulating into a spiral.

method.description: Time is banked rather than rounded, so a frame that takes longer than one step runs several and a short frame runs none; the simulation keeps its fixed rate whatever the frame rate does.

param.name: clock
param.description: Clock to advance; its tick number increases by one.

method.name: CoreNetInterpolatorAdvance
method.brief: Advances the moment being drawn by real time.

param.name: dt
param.description: Seconds since the last call; negative values are ignored.

method.description: The render point runs forward on the client's own clock between snapshots. When it drifts from where it should be, playback is retimed -- run a little fast or a little slow until it lines up -- rather than the point being moved, because moving it makes the whole world jump by the correction. It is snapped only when a long way out, which is a join or a stall, not jitter.
